# AI Teammate — GitHub-issues machine runner (TEMPLATE).
#
# Copy into the TARGET repository (.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml) and
# adapt the RUNNER_* entries. This is the trimmed generic variant of the
# battle-tested machine-kit workflow (see epam/dmtools-dart
# .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml for the full reference with comments).
#
# Two entry paths, and BOTH must survive for the loop to be self-healing:
#   1. issues: [assigned, labeled] — the fast path (labels added with a
#      real PAT fire events; GITHUB_TOKEN-added labels do NOT — that is
#      exactly what the SM cron covers)
#   2. workflow_dispatch (issue / leg / reason) — the SM dispatch path:
#      the reconciler fires this directly, so mute labels cannot stall the
#      loop
#
# The guard derives the leg: dispatch input leg > label agent:rework >
# label agent:review > assignee/agent:dev (dev). Each leg runs the dmtools
# agent config named by RUNNER_*: dev (story/bug) develops from the issue
# body, review produces a machine PR review verdict, rework fixes the
# linked PR by the review threads.
#
# gh-1065/gh-1073: issues events are deduped before the leg fires — one
# human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits MULTIPLE
# issues events, and without the `dedup` probe job each event spawned its
# own teammate run (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061
# three). The probe is transport only; the decision is the unit-tested
# pure module js/common/teammateEventDedup.js, shipped in the agents pack
# the runner leg mounts (dmtools-agents checkout). The probe FAILS OPEN on
# errors, so a broken check never swallows the only trigger.
name: 'AI Teammate'

# Run title carries the EFFECTIVE anchor (owner 2026-09-27, live: dmd run
# 36333172145): a PR-anchored SM dispatch (#544/#687 — inputs.pr set,
# inputs.issue empty) must title '▶ rework (SM) · pr-266', never the
# malformed '▶ rework (SM) · gh- · gh-: '. (inputs.pr || '') guards the
# label-event path, where inputs are null — null != '' would be TRUE and
# render 'pr-' for ordinary issue events.
#
# gh-1065/gh-1073: the issues-event title ALSO carries the LEG — the
# strongest arming label on the issue (rework > review > pr_approved →
# review > dev), not the label written by THIS event: assign-while-labels-
# change emits a bare `assigned` event whose github.event.label.name is
# empty. legOfRunName (js/common/teammateEventDedup.js) parses this emoji
# title family, so a COMPLETED owner stays title-precise: the strict
# completed-owner leg rule (a leg-less completed run never swallows a
# KNOWN new leg) can only work when real leg runs carry their leg here.
run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework') ||
      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review') ||
      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'pr_approved') && '🔍 review') ||
      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:dev') && '⚒️ dev') ||
      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:develop') && '⚒️ dev') ||
      github.event.label.name || '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (#544/#687) — the SM dispatches review/rework with pr instead of issue when the PR has no resolvable LOCAL issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: write

env:
  AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
  # ── adapt per target repo ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  RUNNER_STORY: dmtools-agents/story_development.json
  RUNNER_BUG: dmtools-agents/bug_development.json
  RUNNER_REVIEW: dmtools-agents/pr_review.json
  RUNNER_REWORK: dmtools-agents/pr_rework.json
  DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF: main
  DMTOOLS_VERSION: v0.1.5
  FA_VERSION: latest
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Secrets expected: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT), plus the AI provider key
  # referenced by the runner configs (e.g. ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY).

jobs:
  guard:
    # gh-1029: the `labeled` trigger fires on EVERY label write — including
    # the leg's own lifecycle labels (status:*, ai_developed, ...) — and
    # `on:` cannot filter by label name. Without this job-level gate the
    # guard allocated a runner on each lifecycle-label write only to decide
    # run=false (the self-retrigger no-op burn). `assigned` and the arming
    # `labeled` events (agent:*) still enter; lifecycle labels skip the job
    # entirely and never allocate a runner.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned') ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
      runner: ${{ steps.check.outputs.runner }}
      kind: ${{ steps.check.outputs.kind }}
    steps:
      - name: Decide whether this event is for the agent
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
          ASSIGNEES: ${{ join(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, ' ') }}
          LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}
          INPUT_LEG: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
            LABELS="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')"
            ASSIGNEES="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"
          fi
          state="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state)"
          if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          if echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:skip"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          runner=""
          if [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "rework" ]; then runner="$RUNNER_REWORK";
          elif [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "review" ]; then runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW";
          elif [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "dev" ]; then
            title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then

Actually GitHub expression semantics: `&&` evaluates to the first falsy operand or the last operand (like JS). `contains(...) && '🔧 rework'` — contains returns boolean true → evaluates to '🔧 rework'. Then `a || b || c` — first truthy wins. OK.

4. **The dedup probe job checkout step**: The template's dedup job checks out the entire dmtools-agents pack (full git clone) at `ref: main` (DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF default in template env). Two concerns:

  - **Version skew**: module at `main` vs. the gate in the template. The title content is only issue titles of issues the attacker can create... in a consumer repo, anyone with issue-write can create arbitrary titles → could inject fake workflow commands/annotations. 7. **Bigger functional question — does the dedup actually work for the template given the concurrency group?** Concurrency group: `ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}` — issue-keyed. Second (queued) run starts after first completes: probe sees completed run within 10-min window → drops (if legs compatible). ✓.

8. **A discrepancy between stub and template run-name leg**: The stub title format `teammate: assigned #1040 review` — parsed by stubTailLegOf requiring prefix 'teammate:'. The template title '🔍 review · gh-1040: title' — parsed by emojiLegOf. ✓ Both families supported by module.

9. **Module header note**: "pinned by test_teammateEventDedup.js and test_aiTeammateTemplate.js" — accurate.

10. **Test for priority order**: `reworkAt < reviewAt && reviewAt < devFallbackAt && prApprovedAt < devFallbackAt` — checks prApprovedAt < devFallbackAt but NOT reviewAt < prApprovedAt. Also doesn't check agent:dev/agent:develop before fallback. Test looseness — SUGESTION at most. Actually also: devFallbackAt = indexOf("'⚒️ dev'") — the FIRST occurrence of '⚒️ dev' in the file... where else does '⚒️ dev' occur? Only in run-name (two occurrences: agent:dev leg and the final fallback). indexOf finds the first = the agent:dev mapping. The final fallback '⚒️ dev' is later. So `reviewAt < devFallbackAt` checks review < agent:dev mapping, not review < final fallback. Since the fallback is after all mappings anyway, the test intent is mostly covered. Fine.

11. **`foldedJobIfs` collector matching the guard job's if too**: the dedupIf selection loop takes the LAST if containing 'labeled' without 'needs.dedup' — that's the dedup job gate. Works. But note: if someone reorders jobs (dedup before guard), the test would silently pin the guard gate instead (which lacks the assignee check but the test doesn't assert the assignee containment!). The dedup gate has `contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')` for assigned; the guard gate does not. So the test does NOT pin the assignee check in the dedup gate. Hmm — is that a coverage gap worth noting? 16. **`ref: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF }}`** — env context IS available in `with:` of actions/checkout? Yes, env context is available in jobs.<job_id>.steps.with. ✓

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).

# gh-1073: gh-1065 follow-up: mirror the event-path dedup gate into workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template

## Description

Follow-up to #1065 / #1071 (deferred scope, noted in the PR and in `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` header).

## Why

`workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` is the consumer-repo copy of the AI Teammate stub. PR #1071 added the event-path dedup (the `dedup` probe job + `needs.dedup` gate) to `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` only — every consumer repo still burns duplicate teammate runs on assign-while-labels-change (the live 2026-10-18 evidence: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061 three runs).

## What

- Mirror the gated `dedup` job + the `needs.dedup.outputs.proceed` call gate into the template.
- The template's run titles already carry the leg, and `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (shipped in the agents pack consumers mount) parses them — the pure module slots in directly.
- Consumer repos also need the dedup job's `if:` gate for the gh-1029 zero-burn parity (non-arming label writes must execute zero jobs), and the run-name leg carry (strongest arming label) so completed owners stay title-precise under the strict completed-owner leg rule.

  issues:

        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:

        required: true

  Important subtlety: in GitHub expressions, `&&` returns the second operand when truthy... Actually GitHub expression semantics: `&&` evaluates to the first falsy operand or the last operand (like JS). `contains(...) && '🔧 rework'` — contains returns boolean true → evaluates to '🔧 rework'. Then `a || b || c` — first truthy wins. OK.

3. **Dispatch-path title**: unchanged behavior.

4. **The dedup probe job checkout step**: The template's dedup job checks out the entire dmtools-agents pack (full git clone) at `ref: main` (DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF default in template env). Two concerns:

  - **Version skew**: module at `main` vs. the gate in the template. 6. **Security**: 
  - GH_TOKEN: github.token passed to gh — read-only GET calls. The workflow has `actions: write` etc. permissions at workflow level, token scope not reduced for the probe. Parity with stub. Fine.

  - Audit echo: run names include issue titles (attacker-controllable in theory). `out()` collapses whitespace — prevents GITHUB_OUTPUT multi-line injection. ✓ Good.
  - `::warning::`/`::notice::` console with title content — GitHub runner blocks command injection from `::` in log lines? Modern runners (v2.2xx+) do NOT automatically escape `::` in echo; there's a known GHSL advisory about workflow commands injection via untrusted content. The recommended mitigation is env-var wrapping. Here the audit line embeds run names (which contain issue titles) into a `::warning::` line. If an issue title contained something like `::error::` or worse `::set-output`... set-output is disabled. `::error file=...` could fake annotations. Let me check the stub — identical. Since stub is merged, parity is desired; a SUGESTION is fair but arguably noise. The title content is only issue titles of issues the attacker can create... in a consumer repo, anyone with issue-write can create arbitrary titles → could inject fake workflow commands/annotations. Low severity. I'll mention as SUGESTION.

7. **Bigger functional question — does the dedup actually work for the template given the concurrency group?** Concurrency group: `ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}` — issue-keyed. Burst duplicates queue. First run executes probe: sees no older runs → proceed. Second (queued) run starts after first completes: probe sees completed run within 10-min window → drops (if legs compatible). ✓.

8. **A discrepancy between stub and template run-name leg**: The stub title format `teammate: assigned #1040 review` — parsed by stubTailLegOf requiring prefix 'teammate:'. The template title '🔍 review · gh-1040: title' — parsed by emojiLegOf. ✓ Both families supported by module.

9. **Module header note**: "pinned by test_teammateEventDedup.js and test_aiTeammateTemplate.js" — accurate.

10. **Test for priority order**: `reworkAt < reviewAt && reviewAt < devFallbackAt && prApprovedAt < devFallbackAt` — checks prApprovedAt < devFallbackAt but NOT reviewAt < prApprovedAt. Also doesn't check agent:dev/agent:develop before fallback. Test looseness — SUGESTION at most. Actually also: devFallbackAt = indexOf("'⚒️ dev'") — the FIRST occurrence of '⚒️ dev' in the file... where else does '⚒️ dev' occur? Only in run-name (two occurrences: agent:dev leg and the final fallback). indexOf finds the first = the agent:dev mapping. The final fallback '⚒️ dev' is later. So `reviewAt < devFallbackAt` checks review < agent:dev mapping, not review < final fallback. Since the fallback is after all mappings anyway, the test intent is mostly covered. Fine.

11. **`foldedJobIfs` collector matching the guard job's if too**: the dedupIf selection loop takes the LAST if containing 'labeled' without 'needs.dedup' — that's the dedup job gate. Works. But note: if someone reorders jobs (dedup before guard), the test would silently pin the guard gate instead (which lacks the assignee check but the test doesn't assert the assignee containment!). The dedup gate has `contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')` for assigned; the guard gate does not. The test asserts dedupIf contains "github.event.action == 'assigned'" — both satisfy. So the test would pass even if the dedup gate lost its assignee check... wait no — if the dedup gate lost the assignee check, then dedupIf (the dedup gate, containing labeled) would still pass the test because it only checks 'assigned' presence. So the test does NOT pin the assignee check in the dedup gate. Hmm — is that a coverage gap worth noting? The stub's own test (test_teammateEventDedup.js / test_workflowLint.js) may pin the stub gate. Let me check what test_workflowLint pins about the template. There's a test 'the dedup gate keys the assignee check to the assigned action' — asserts presence of 'assigned' only. But the gh-1029 zero-burn parity claim ("assigned requires the ai-teammate assignee") would be violated — the probe would burn a runner per non-teammate assignment. That's a real coverage gap in the test. SUGESTION-level: tighten the test to assert the assignee check in dedupIf. Let me verify the diff hunk line for this assertion to reference inline.

15. One more check — **the template's dedup job in a consumer repo without the pack secrets**: checkout of IstiN/dmtools-agents is public → fine without token.

16. **`ref: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF }}`** — env context IS available in `with:` of actions/checkout? Yes, env context is available in jobs.<job_id>.steps.with. ✓

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## Description

Follow-up to #1065 / #1071 (deferred scope, noted in the PR and in `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` header).

## Why

`workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` is the consumer-repo copy of the AI Teammate stub. PR #1071 added the event-path dedup (the `dedup` probe job + `needs.dedup` gate) to `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` only — every consumer repo still burns duplicate teammate runs on assign-while-labels-change (the live 2026-10-18 evidence: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061 three runs).

- Mirror the gated `dedup` job + the `needs.dedup.outputs.proceed` call gate into the template.

    "description": "Follow-up to #1065 / #1071 (deferred scope, noted in the PR and in `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` header).

## Why

`workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` is the consumer-repo copy of the AI Teammate stub. PR #1071 added the event-path dedup (the `dedup` probe job + `needs.dedup` gate) to `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` only — every consumer repo still burns duplicate teammate runs on assign-while-labels-change (the live 2026-10-18 evidence: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061 three runs).

## What

- Mirror the gated `dedup` job + the `needs.dedup.outputs.proceed` call gate into the template.
- The template's run titles already carry the leg, and `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (shipped in the agents pack consumers mount) parses them — the pure module slots in directly.

diff --git a/workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template b/workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template
index afb26513..369e515a 100644
--- a/workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template
+++ b/workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template
@@ -18,6 +18,15 @@
 # agent config named by RUNNER_*: dev (story/bug) develops from the issue
 # body, review produces a machine PR review verdict, rework fixes the
 # linked PR by the review threads.
+#
+# gh-1065/gh-1073: issues events are deduped before the leg fires — one
+# human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits MULTIPLE
+# issues events, and without the `dedup` probe job each event spawned its
+# own teammate run (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061
+# three). The probe is transport only; the decision is the unit-tested
+# pure module js/common/teammateEventDedup.js, shipped in the agents pack
+# the runner leg mounts (dmtools-agents checkout). The probe FAILS OPEN on
+# errors, so a broken check never swallows the only trigger.
 name: 'AI Teammate'
 
 # Run title carries the EFFECTIVE anchor (owner 2026-09-27, live: dmd run
@@ -26,14 +35,26 @@ name: 'AI Teammate'
 # malformed '▶ rework (SM) · gh- · gh-: '. (inputs.pr || '') guards the
 # label-event path, where inputs are null — null != '' would be TRUE and
 # render 'pr-' for ordinary issue events.
+#
+# gh-1065/gh-1073: the issues-event title ALSO carries the LEG — the
+# strongest arming label on the issue (rework > review > pr_approved →
+# review > dev), not the label written by THIS event: assign-while-labels-
+# change emits a bare `assigned` event whose github.event.label.name is
+# empty. legOfRunName (js/common/teammateEventDedup.js) parses this emoji
+# title family, so a COMPLETED owner stays title-precise: the strict
+# completed-owner leg rule (a leg-less completed run never swallows a
+# KNOWN new leg) can only work when real leg runs carry their leg here.
 run-name: >-
   ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
         (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
         || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
-      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
-      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
-      '⚒️ dev' }}
+      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework') ||
+      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review') ||
+      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'pr_approved') && '🔍 review') ||
+      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:dev') && '⚒️ dev') ||
+      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:develop') && '⚒️ dev') ||
+      github.event.label.name || '⚒️ dev' }}
   · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
       || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
       github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}
@@ -165,9 +186,206 @@ jobs:
             echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
           fi
 
+  # gh-1065/gh-1073: event-path dedup probe (the engine repo's stub carries
+  # the same job — see .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml). One human action
+  # (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits MULTIPLE issues events and
+  # each event started its own teammate run — two per issue, three on #1061,
+  # the owner hand-cancelling duplicates. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM
+  # dispatch path only; this job is the missing event-path gate. It probes
+  # the repo's ai-teammate.yml runs (per-status gh api fan-out, smAgent
+  # parity) and lets the `teammate` call fire only when no OLDER run for
+  # the same issue + leg is in flight or freshly completed. Probe errors
+  # FAIL OPEN (AC3): a broken check writes proceed=true so the only trigger
+  # of a burst is never silently swallowed. The decision itself is the
+  # unit-tested pure module js/common/teammateEventDedup.js (AC4) — this
+  # step is transport only. The probe short-circuits BEFORE any API call
+  # for workflow_dispatch (SM-side gh-1028 governs it), non-arming
+  # lifecycle labels and non-teammate assignees.
+  dedup:
+    name: Event-path dedup probe (gh-1065)
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    # gh-1029 zero-burn parity: this gate MIRRORS the guard gate above.
+    # `on:` fires on EVERY label write repo-wide, and an unguarded dedup
+    # job would allocate a runner (pack checkout + node boot) per
+    # lifecycle-label storm — the exact burn gh-1029 eliminated. Rejected
+    # events execute ZERO jobs: the run concludes failure (the gh-676
+    # phantom pattern) and — because only conclusion 'success' owns the
+    # freshness window — can never suppress a trigger for an issue whose
+    # leg never ran. NOTE: a job-level `if:` cannot read the env block —
+    # if you retarget AGENT_HANDLE below, mirror it into the two
+    # 'ai-teammate' literals in this gate and the teammate call gate.
+    if: >-
+      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
+      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
+       github.event.action == 'assigned' &&
+       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
+      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
+       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
+       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
+        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
+        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
+        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
+        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
+    outputs:
+      proceed: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.proceed }}
+      audit: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.audit }}
+    steps:
+      # The pure decision module ships in the agents pack (the runner leg
+      # below mounts the same checkout) — the consumer repo tree does NOT
+      # carry js/common/. Same DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF pin as the runner leg.
+      - name: Checkout dmtools-agents (dedup decision module)
+        uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          repository: IstiN/dmtools-agents
+          ref: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF }}
+          path: dmtools-agents
+      - id: probe
+        name: Decide whether this event duplicates an in-flight teammate run
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
+          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
+          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
+          LABEL_NAME: ${{ github.event.label.name }}
+          ISSUE_LABELS: ${{ toJson(github.event.issue.labels.*.name) }}
+          ISSUE: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
+          ASSIGNEES: ${{ toJson(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login) }}
+          SELF_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
+          SELF_RUN_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
+          WORKFLOW_FILE: ai-teammate.yml
+          # GITHUB_OUTPUT is provided by the runner — do NOT set it here.

# AI Teammate — GitHub-issues machine runner (TEMPLATE).
#
# Copy into the TARGET repository (.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml) and
# adapt the RUNNER_* entries. This is the trimmed generic variant of the
# battle-tested machine-kit workflow (see epam/dmtools-dart
# .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml for the full reference with comments).
#
# Two entry paths, and BOTH must survive for the loop to be self-healing:
#   1. issues: [assigned, labeled] — the fast path (labels added with a
#      real PAT fire events; GITHUB_TOKEN-added labels do NOT — that is
#      exactly what the SM cron covers)
#   2. workflow_dispatch (issue / leg / reason) — the SM dispatch path:
#      the reconciler fires this directly, so mute labels cannot stall the
#      loop

# The guard derives the leg: dispatch input leg > label agent:rework >
# label agent:review > assignee/agent:dev (dev). Each leg runs the dmtools
# agent config named by RUNNER_*: dev (story/bug) develops from the issue
# body, review produces a machine PR review verdict, rework fixes the
# linked PR by the review threads.
#
# gh-1065/gh-1073: issues events are deduped before the leg fires — one
# human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits MULTIPLE
# issues events, and without the `dedup` probe job each event spawned its
# own teammate run (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061
# three). The probe is transport only; the decision is the unit-tested
# pure module js/common/teammateEventDedup.js, shipped in the agents pack
# the runner leg mounts (dmtools-agents checkout). The probe FAILS OPEN on
# errors, so a broken check never swallows the only trigger.
name: 'AI Teammate'

# 36333172145): a PR-anchored SM dispatch (#544/#687 — inputs.pr set,

# label-event path, where inputs are null — null != '' would be TRUE and
# render 'pr-' for ordinary issue events.

# gh-1065/gh-1073: the issues-event title ALSO carries the LEG — the
# strongest arming label on the issue (rework > review > pr_approved →
# review > dev), not the label written by THIS event: assign-while-labels-
# change emits a bare `assigned` event whose github.event.label.name is
# empty. legOfRunName (js/common/teammateEventDedup.js) parses this emoji
# title family, so a COMPLETED owner stays title-precise: the strict
# completed-owner leg rule (a leg-less completed run never swallows a
# KNOWN new leg) can only work when real leg runs carry their leg here.

      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:dev') && '⚒️ dev') ||
      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:develop') && '⚒️ dev') ||
      github.event.label.name || '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:

      issue:

        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:

        required: true

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: write

Actually GitHub expression semantics: `&&` evaluates to the first falsy operand or the last operand (like JS). `contains(...) && '🔧 rework'` — contains returns boolean true → evaluates to '🔧 rework'. Then `a || b || c` — first truthy wins. OK.

4. **The dedup probe job checkout step**: The template's dedup job checks out the entire dmtools-agents pack (full git clone) at `ref: main` (DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF default in template env). Two concerns:

Let me check the stub — identical. Since stub is merged, parity is desired; a SUGESTION is fair but arguably noise. The title content is only issue titles of issues the attacker can create... in a consumer repo, anyone with issue-write can create arbitrary titles → could inject fake workflow commands/annotations. Low severity. I'll mention as SUGESTION.

7. **Bigger functional question — does the dedup actually work for the template given the concurrency group?** Concurrency group: `ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}` — issue-keyed. Burst duplicates queue. First run executes probe: sees no older runs → proceed. Second (queued) run starts after first completes: probe sees completed run within 10-min window → drops (if legs compatible). ✓.

10. **Test for priority order**: `reworkAt < reviewAt && reviewAt < devFallbackAt && prApprovedAt < devFallbackAt` — checks prApprovedAt < devFallbackAt but NOT reviewAt < prApprovedAt. Also doesn't check agent:dev/agent:develop before fallback. Test looseness — SUGESTION at most. Actually also: devFallbackAt = indexOf("'⚒️ dev'") — the FIRST occurrence of '⚒️ dev' in the file... where else does '⚒️ dev' occur? Only in run-name (two occurrences: agent:dev leg and the final fallback). indexOf finds the first = the agent:dev mapping. The final fallback '⚒️ dev' is later. So `reviewAt < devFallbackAt` checks review < agent:dev mapping, not review < final fallback. Since the fallback is after all mappings anyway, the test intent is mostly covered. Fine.

# gh-1073: gh-1065 follow-up: mirror the event-path dedup gate into workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template

## Description

Follow-up to #1065 / #1071 (deferred scope, noted in the PR and in `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` header).

## Why

`workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` is the consumer-repo copy of the AI Teammate stub. PR #1071 added the event-path dedup (the `dedup` probe job + `needs.dedup` gate) to `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` only — every consumer repo still burns duplicate teammate runs on assign-while-labels-change (the live 2026-10-18 evidence: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061 three runs).

## What

- Mirror the gated `dedup` job + the `needs.dedup.outputs.proceed` call gate into the template.
- The template's run titles already carry the leg, and `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (shipped in the agents pack consumers mount) parses them — the pure module slots in directly.
- Consumer repos also need the dedup job's `if:` gate for the gh-1029 zero-burn parity (non-arming label writes must execute zero jobs), and the run-name leg carry (strongest arming label) so completed owners stay title-precise under the strict completed-owner leg rule.

# AI Teammate — GitHub-issues machine runner (TEMPLATE).
#
# Copy into the TARGET repository (.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml) and
# adapt the RUNNER_* entries. This is the trimmed generic variant of the
# battle-tested machine-kit workflow (see epam/dmtools-dart
# .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml for the full reference with comments).
#
# Two entry paths, and BOTH must survive for the loop to be self-healing:
#   1. issues: [assigned, labeled] — the fast path (labels added with a
#      real PAT fire events; GITHUB_TOKEN-added labels do NOT — that is
#      exactly what the SM cron covers)
#   2. workflow_dispatch (issue / leg / reason) — the SM dispatch path:
#      the reconciler fires this directly, so mute labels cannot stall the
#      loop
#
# The guard derives the leg: dispatch input leg > label agent:rework >
# label agent:review > assignee/agent:dev (dev). Each leg runs the dmtools
# agent config named by RUNNER_*: dev (story/bug) develops from the issue
# body, review produces a machine PR review verdict, rework fixes the
# linked PR by the review threads.
#
# gh-1065/gh-1073: issues events are deduped before the leg fires — one
# human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits MULTIPLE
# issues events, and without the `dedup` probe job each event spawned its
# own teammate run (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061
# three). The probe is transport only; the decision is the unit-tested
# pure module js/common/teammateEventDedup.js, shipped in the agents pack
# the runner leg mounts (dmtools-agents checkout). The probe FAILS OPEN on
# errors, so a broken check never swallows the only trigger.
name: 'AI Teammate'

# Run title carries the EFFECTIVE anchor (owner 2026-09-27, live: dmd run
# 36333172145): a PR-anchored SM dispatch (#544/#687 — inputs.pr set,
# inputs.issue empty) must title '▶ rework (SM) · pr-266', never the
# malformed '▶ rework (SM) · gh- · gh-: '. (inputs.pr || '') guards the
# label-event path, where inputs are null — null != '' would be TRUE and
# render 'pr-' for ordinary issue events.
#
# gh-1065/gh-1073: the issues-event title ALSO carries the LEG — the
# strongest arming label on the issue (rework > review > pr_approved →
# review > dev), not the label written by THIS event: assign-while-labels-
# change emits a bare `assigned` event whose github.event.label.name is
# empty. legOfRunName (js/common/teammateEventDedup.js) parses this emoji
# title family, so a COMPLETED owner stays title-precise: the strict
# completed-owner leg rule (a leg-less completed run never swallows a
# KNOWN new leg) can only work when real leg runs carry their leg here.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `emojiLegOf` marker-priority scan can mis-parse a template run title when the issue title contains a stronger marker**

This PR activates the emoji title family for the dedup decision in consumer repos: the probe's `legOfRunName` now parses titles like `⚒️ dev · gh-9: <issue title>`, where the trailing `<issue title>` is user-controlled. The module's `emojiLegOf` (`js/common/teammateEventDedup.js`) iterates `EMOJI_LEG_MARKERS` in priority order (`🔧` → `🔍` → `⚒️`) over the **whole** name, not anchored to the leading leg token — so a title containing a stronger marker shadows the real leg. Verified live against this branch's module:

```javascript
m.legOfRunName('⚒️ dev · gh-9: 🔧 rework the parser'); // → "rework" (real leg: dev)
m.legOfRunName('🔍 review · gh-9: fix things');        // → "review" ✓
```

The stub titles (`teammate: ... #<n> <leg>`, trailing-token parse, no issue title embedded) do not have this hazard — it is specific to the template title family this PR wires into the decision. Impact is narrow but real, in the swallow-a-trigger direction the strict completed-owner rule exists to prevent: a dev-leg run completes on an issue whose title contains `🔧 rework`, and a genuine `agent:review` label write within the 10-min freshness window is attributed leg `rework` → `completedLegsCompatible('review','rework')` is false → **not** suppressed (this direction only re-burns a run), while a `pr_approved`-driven review event *would* match the misread `review` leg and be silently dropped.

Suggested fix (module side, keeps both title families working): anchor the emoji scan to the name start — the leg token is always the first token of an issues-event template title — e.g. test markers only in the substring before the first `·`, or check `name.indexOf(marker) === 0` priority-wise. Could you confirm whether you want this tightened here or as a follow-up? If you consider a marker-emoji issue title too adversarial to guard, happy to downgrade to a documented limitation.

💡 **SUGGESTION: pin the assignee clause in the dedup-gate assertion**

The `dedupIf` selector takes the **last** folded `if: >-` block that mentions `labeled` and not `needs.dedup`, and the assertions check the arming labels, `action == 'assigned'` and the dispatch path — but never the assignee containment. Two gaps follow:

1. If the `dedup` job's gate lost its `contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')` clause (keeping everything else), this test would still pass — yet every non-teammate assignment in a consumer repo would allocate a probe runner (pack checkout + node boot), the exact gh-1029 zero-burn regression class this PR fixes.
2. If job order ever changes so the `guard` job's gate comes last, the selector silently pins the **guard** gate (which has no assignee check), and gap 1 applies again.

The teammate-call gate's assignee clause is pinned by `test_workflowLint.js`, but the probe job's own zero-burn gate is only covered here. Consider:

```javascript
assert.ok(dedupIf.indexOf("contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')") !== -1,
    'the dedup gate admits assigned events ONLY for the ai-teammate assignee (gh-1029 zero-burn parity)');
```

That assertion also disambiguates the selector: the guard gate would fail it, so a reorder or a copy-pasted gate gets caught instead of silently passing.

💡 **SUGGESTION: sparse-checkout the pack — the probe needs exactly one file**

The dedup job clones the whole `dmtools-agents` pack on **every** arming event (and every dispatch) just to `require` a single module. It is a shallow clone (`fetch-depth: 1` default), but the tree is still several thousand files that are never read. Since this job exists to eliminate runner burn, it could eat its own cooking:

```yaml
      - name: Checkout dmtools-agents (dedup decision module)
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: IstiN/dmtools-agents
          ref: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF }}
          path: dmtools-agents
          sparse-checkout: js/common/teammateEventDedup.js
```

The require path is unchanged (`./dmtools-agents/js/common/teammateEventDedup.js`). Optional — merge as-is is fine; worth it only because the template is copied into many consumer repos, so the saving multiplies.

# gh-1073: gh-1065 follow-up: mirror the event-path dedup gate into workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template

## Description

Follow-up to #1065 / #1071 (deferred scope, noted in the PR and in `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` header).

## Why

`workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` is the consumer-repo copy of the AI Teammate stub. PR #1071 added the event-path dedup (the `dedup` probe job + `needs.dedup` gate) to `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` only — every consumer repo still burns duplicate teammate runs on assign-while-labels-change (the live 2026-10-18 evidence: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061 three runs).

## What

- Mirror the gated `dedup` job + the `needs.dedup.outputs.proceed` call gate into the template.
- The template's run titles already carry the leg, and `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (shipped in the agents pack consumers mount) parses them — the pure module slots in directly.
- Consumer repos also need the dedup job's `if:` gate for the gh-1029 zero-burn parity (non-arming label writes must execute zero jobs), and the run-name leg carry (strongest arming label) so completed owners stay title-precise under the strict completed-owner leg rule.

# AI Teammate — GitHub-issues machine runner (TEMPLATE).
#
# Copy into the TARGET repository (.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml) and
# adapt the RUNNER_* entries. This is the trimmed generic variant of the
# battle-tested machine-kit workflow (see epam/dmtools-dart
# .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml for the full reference with comments).
#
# Two entry paths, and BOTH must survive for the loop to be self-healing:
#   1. issues: [assigned, labeled] — the fast path (labels added with a
#      real PAT fire events; GITHUB_TOKEN-added labels do NOT — that is
#      exactly what the SM cron covers)
#   2. workflow_dispatch (issue / leg / reason) — the SM dispatch path:
#      the reconciler fires this directly, so mute labels cannot stall the
#      loop
#
# The guard derives the leg: dispatch input leg > label agent:rework >
# label agent:review > assignee/agent:dev (dev). Each leg runs the dmtools
# agent config named by RUNNER_*: dev (story/bug) develops from the issue
# body, review produces a machine PR review verdict, rework fixes the
# linked PR by the review threads.
#
# gh-1065/gh-1073: issues events are deduped before the leg fires — one
# human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits MULTIPLE
# issues events, and without the `dedup` probe job each event spawned its
# own teammate run (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061
# three). The probe is transport only; the decision is the unit-tested
# pure module js/common/teammateEventDedup.js, shipped in the agents pack
# the runner leg mounts (dmtools-agents checkout). The probe FAILS OPEN on
# errors, so a broken check never swallows the only trigger.
name: 'AI Teammate'

# Run title carries the EFFECTIVE anchor (owner 2026-09-27, live: dmd run
# 36333172145): a PR-anchored SM dispatch (#544/#687 — inputs.pr set,
# inputs.issue empty) must title '▶ rework (SM) · pr-266', never the
# malformed '▶ rework (SM) · gh- · gh-: '. (inputs.pr || '') guards the
# label-event path, where inputs are null — null != '' would be TRUE and
# render 'pr-' for ordinary issue events.
#
# gh-1065/gh-1073: the issues-event title ALSO carries the LEG — the
# strongest arming label on the issue (rework > review > pr_approved →
# review > dev), not the label written by THIS event: assign-while-labels-
# change emits a bare `assigned` event whose github.event.label.name is
# empty. legOfRunName (js/common/teammateEventDedup.js) parses this emoji
# title family, so a COMPLETED owner stays title-precise: the strict
# completed-owner leg rule (a leg-less completed run never swallows a
# KNOWN new leg) can only work when real leg runs carry their leg here.
run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework') ||
      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review') ||
      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'pr_approved') && '🔍 review') ||
      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:dev') && '⚒️ dev') ||
      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:develop') && '⚒️ dev') ||
      github.event.label.name || '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (#544/#687) — the SM dispatches review/rework with pr instead of issue when the PR has no resolvable LOCAL issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: write

env:
  AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
  # ── adapt per target repo ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  RUNNER_STORY: dmtools-agents/story_development.json
  RUNNER_BUG: dmtools-agents/bug_development.json
  RUNNER_REVIEW: dmtools-agents/pr_review.json
  RUNNER_REWORK: dmtools-agents/pr_rework.json
  DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF: main
  DMTOOLS_VERSION: v0.1.5
  FA_VERSION: latest
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Secrets expected: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT), plus the AI provider key
  # referenced by the runner configs (e.g. ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY).

jobs:
  guard:
    # gh-1029: the `labeled` trigger fires on EVERY label write — including
    # the leg's own lifecycle labels (status:*, ai_developed, ...) — and
    # `on:` cannot filter by label name. Without this job-level gate the
    # guard allocated a runner on each lifecycle-label write only to decide
    # run=false (the self-retrigger no-op burn). `assigned` and the arming
    # `labeled` events (agent:*) still enter; lifecycle labels skip the job
    # entirely and never allocate a runner.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned') ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
      runner: ${{ steps.check.outputs.runner }}
      kind: ${{ steps.check.outputs.kind }}
    steps:
      - name: Decide whether this event is for the agent
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
          ASSIGNEES: ${{ join(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, ' ') }}
          LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}
          INPUT_LEG: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
            LABELS="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')"
            ASSIGNEES="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"
          fi
          state="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state)"
          if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          if echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:skip"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          runner=""
          if [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "rework" ]; then runner="$RUNNER_REWORK";
          elif [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "review" ]; then runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW";
          elif [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "dev" ]; then
            title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then

# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

# leg directly, and for event-path runs the strongest arming label on the
# issue (rework > review > pr_approved → review > dev). legOfRunName

# COMPLETED owner stays title-precise: the strict completed-owner leg rule
# (a leg-less completed run never swallows a KNOWN new leg) can only work
# when real leg runs carry their leg in the title.

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false

permissions:

  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-

  actions: write
  contents: write

  pull-requests: write

concurrency:

blocks.text:
The PR's verification claims check out locally (12/40/30). Now let me do the deep analysis for issues. Let me think about the diff hunks and hunt for actual problems.

Key analysis points:

1. **Template run-name change**: Before: `github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' || ...`. After: `contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' || ...`. 

  Important subtlety: in GitHub expressions, `&&` returns the second operand when truthy... Actually GitHub expression semantics: `&&` evaluates to the first falsy operand or the last operand (like JS). `contains(...) && '🔧 rework'` — contains returns boolean true → evaluates to '🔧 rework'. Then `a || b || c` — first truthy wins. OK.

  One subtlety: the old behavior titled a `labeled agent:rework` event '🔧 rework' even if the label was subsequently removed... irrelevant.

  New behavior for labeled events: uses issue.labels (current state at event time — the payload's labels array includes the newly added label). Fine.

2. **`github.event.label.name || '⚒️ dev'` fallback**: For a `labeled` event with a non-arming label that somehow reaches here (zero jobs anyway, so run-name still renders). Not an issue.

3. **Dispatch-path title**: unchanged behavior.

4. **The dedup probe job checkout step**: The template's dedup job checks out the entire dmtools-agents pack (full git clone) at `ref: main` (DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF default in template env). Two concerns:
  - **Cost**: full clone per arming event. Minor.
  - **Version skew**: module at `main` vs. the gate in the template. The template is copied into consumer repos, possibly older; a breaking change to the module's API on main would break consumer probes. But fail-open catch-all means dedup silently disables. Acceptable design, and the PR explicitly pins the probe to the same ref as the runner leg (parity).

5. **A potential REAL issue — the template probe runs before any checkout of the consumer repo**: actions/checkout with `path: dmtools-agents` only checks out the pack. require path is relative to cwd ($GITHUB_WORKSPACE). Pack lands at $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/dmtools-agents. ✓ works.

6. **Security**: 
  - GH_TOKEN: github.token passed to gh — read-only GET calls. The workflow has `actions: write` etc. permissions at workflow level, token scope not reduced for the probe. Parity with stub. Fine.
  - `ISSUE_LABELS`/`ASSIGNES` JSON → parsed safely. 
  - `${env.REPO}` into execFileSync args array (not shell) — no injection. ✓
  - Audit echo: run names include issue titles (attacker-controllable in theory). `out()` collapses whitespace — prevents GITHUB_OUTPUT multi-line injection. ✓ Good.
  - `::warning::`/`::notice::` console with title content — GitHub runner blocks command injection from `::` in log lines? Modern runners (v2.2xx+) do NOT automatically escape `::` in echo; there's a known GHSL advisory about workflow commands injection via untrusted content. The recommended mitigation is env-var wrapping. Here the audit line embeds run names (which contain issue titles) into a `::warning::` line. If an issue title contained something like `::error::` or worse `::set-output`... set-output is disabled. `::error file=...` could fake annotations. This is the same pattern as the stub (already merged via PR #1071). It's a pre-existing parity concern; could raise as SUGESTION on the template line where the console.log happens. Let me check the stub — identical. Since stub is merged, parity is desired; a SUGESTION is fair but arguably noise. The title content is only issue titles of issues the attacker can create... in a consumer repo, anyone with issue-write can create arbitrary titles → could inject fake workflow commands/annotations. Low severity. I'll mention as SUGESTION.

7. **Bigger functional question — does the dedup actually work for the template given the concurrency group?** Concurrency group: `ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}` — issue-keyed. Burst duplicates queue. First run executes probe: sees no older runs → proceed. Second (queued) run starts after first completes: probe sees completed run within 10-min window → drops (if legs compatible). ✓.

8. **A discrepancy between stub and template run-name leg**: The stub title format `teammate: assigned #1040 review` — parsed by stubTailLegOf requiring prefix 'teammate:'. The template title '🔍 review · gh-1040: title' — parsed by emojiLegOf. ✓ Both families supported by module.

9. **Module header note**: "pinned by test_teammateEventDedup.js and test_aiTeammateTemplate.js" — accurate.

10. **Test for priority order**: `reworkAt < reviewAt && reviewAt < devFallbackAt && prApprovedAt < devFallbackAt` — checks prApprovedAt < devFallbackAt but NOT reviewAt < prApprovedAt. Also doesn't check agent:dev/agent:develop before fallback. Test looseness — SUGESTION at most. Actually also: devFallbackAt = indexOf("'⚒️ dev'") — the FIRST occurrence of '⚒️ dev' in the file... where else does '⚒️ dev' occur? Only in run-name (two occurrences: agent:dev leg and the final fallback). indexOf finds the first = the agent:dev mapping. The final fallback '⚒️ dev' is later. So `reviewAt < devFallbackAt` checks review < agent:dev mapping, not review < final fallback. Since the fallback is after all mappings anyway, the test intent is mostly covered. Fine.

11. **`foldedJobIfs` collector matching the guard job's if too**: the dedupIf selection loop takes the LAST if containing 'labeled' without 'needs.dedup' — that's the dedup job gate. Works. But note: if someone reorders jobs (dedup before guard), the test would silently pin the guard gate instead (which lacks the assignee check but the test doesn't assert the assignee containment!). The dedup gate has `contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')` for assigned; the guard gate does not. The test asserts dedupIf contains "github.event.action == 'assigned'" — both satisfy. So the test would pass even if the dedup gate lost its assignee check... wait no — if the dedup gate lost the assignee check, then dedupIf (the dedup gate, containing labeled) would still pass the test because it only checks 'assigned' presence. So the test does NOT pin the assignee check in the dedup gate. Hmm — is that a coverage gap worth noting? The stub's own test (test_teammateEventDedup.js / test_workflowLint.js) may pin the stub gate. Let me check what test_workflowLint pins about the template. There's a test 'the dedup gate keys the assignee check to the assigned action' — asserts presence of 'assigned' only. The actual functional consequence: if dedup gate admitted ALL assigned events (like the guard gate), then an assigned event not to ai-teammate would run the dedup job → probe preflight checks assignees and proceeds → no burn beyond the probe job allocation. But the gh-1029 zero-burn parity claim ("assigned requires the ai-teammate assignee") would be violated — the probe would burn a runner per non-teammate assignment. {"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `emojiLegOf` marker-priority scan can mis-parse a template run title when the issue title contains a stronger marker**

This PR activates the emoji title family for the dedup decision in consumer repos: the probe's `legOfRunName` now parses titles like `⚒️ dev · gh-9: <issue title>`, where the trailing `<issue title>` is user-controlled. The module's `emojiLegOf` (`js/common/teammateEventDedup.js`) iterates `EMOJI_LEG_MARKERS` in priority order (`🔧` → `🔍` → `⚒️`) over the **whole** name, not anchored to the leading leg token — so a title containing a stronger marker shadows the real leg. Verified live against this branch's module:

```javascript
m.legOfRunName('⚒️ dev · gh-9: 🔧 rework the parser'); // → "rework" (real leg: dev)
m.legOfRunName('🔍 review · gh-9: fix things');        // → "review" ✓
```

The stub titles (`teammate: ... #<n> <leg>`, trailing-token parse, no issue title embedded) do not have this hazard — it is specific to the template title family this PR wires into the decision. Impact is narrow but real, in the swallow-a-trigger direction the strict completed-owner rule exists to prevent: a dev-leg run completes on an issue whose title contains `🔧 rework`, and a genuine `agent:review` label write within the 10-min freshness window is attributed leg `rework` → `completedLegsCompatible('review','rework')` is false → **not** suppressed (this direction only re-burns a run), while a `pr_approved`-driven review event *would* match the misread `review` leg and be silently dropped.

Suggested fix (module side, keeps both title families working): anchor the emoji scan to the name start — the leg token is always the first token of an issues-event template title — e.g. test markers only in the substring before the first `·`, or check `name.indexOf(marker) === 0` priority-wise. Could you confirm whether you want this tightened here or as a follow-up? If you consider a marker-emoji issue title too adversarial to guard, happy to downgrade to a documented limitation.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: pin the assignee clause in the dedup-gate assertion**

The `dedupIf` selector takes the **last** folded `if: >-` block that mentions `labeled` and not `needs.dedup`, and the assertions check the arming labels, `action == 'assigned'` and the dispatch path — but never the assignee containment. Two gaps follow:

1. If the `dedup` job's gate lost its `contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')` clause (keeping everything else), this test would still pass — yet every non-teammate assignment in a consumer repo would allocate a probe runner (pack checkout + node boot), the exact gh-1029 zero-burn regression class this PR fixes.
2. If job order ever changes so the `guard` job's gate comes last, the selector silently pins the **guard** gate (which has no assignee check), and gap 1 applies again.

The teammate-call gate's assignee clause is pinned by `test_workflowLint.js`, but the probe job's own zero-burn gate is only covered here. Consider:

```javascript
assert.ok(dedupIf.indexOf("contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')") !== -1,
    'the dedup gate admits assigned events ONLY for the ai-teammate assignee (gh-1029 zero-burn parity)');
```

That assertion also disambiguates the selector: the guard gate would fail it, so a reorder or a copy-pasted gate gets caught instead of silently passing.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: sparse-checkout the pack — the probe needs exactly one file**

The dedup job clones the whole `dmtools-agents` pack on **every** arming event (and every dispatch) just to `require` a single module. It is a shallow clone (`fetch-depth: 1` default), but the tree is still several thousand files that are never read. Since this job exists to eliminate runner burn, it could eat its own cooking:

      - name: Checkout dmtools-agents (dedup decision module)

          ref: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF }}

```

The require path is unchanged (`./dmtools-agents/js/common/teammateEventDedup.js`). Optional — merge as-is is fine; worth it only because the template is copied into many consumer repos, so the saving multiplies.

# gh-1073: gh-1065 follow-up: mirror the event-path dedup gate into workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template

## Description

Follow-up to #1065 / #1071 (deferred scope, noted in the PR and in `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` header).

## Why

`workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` is the consumer-repo copy of the AI Teammate stub. PR #1071 added the event-path dedup (the `dedup` probe job + `needs.dedup` gate) to `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` only — every consumer repo still burns duplicate teammate runs on assign-while-labels-change (the live 2026-10-18 evidence: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061 three runs).

## What

- Mirror the gated `dedup` job + the `needs.dedup.outputs.proceed` call gate into the template.
- The template's run titles already carry the leg, and `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (shipped in the agents pack consumers mount) parses them — the pure module slots in directly.
- Consumer repos also need the dedup job's `if:` gate for the gh-1029 zero-burn parity (non-arming label writes must execute zero jobs), and the run-name leg carry (strongest arming label) so completed owners stay title-precise under the strict completed-owner leg rule.

# AI Teammate — GitHub-issues machine runner (TEMPLATE).
#
# Copy into the TARGET repository (.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml) and
# adapt the RUNNER_* entries. This is the trimmed generic variant of the
# battle-tested machine-kit workflow (see epam/dmtools-dart
# .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml for the full reference with comments).
#
# Two entry paths, and BOTH must survive for the loop to be self-healing:
#   1. issues: [assigned, labeled] — the fast path (labels added with a
#      real PAT fire events; GITHUB_TOKEN-added labels do NOT — that is
#      exactly what the SM cron covers)
#   2. workflow_dispatch (issue / leg / reason) — the SM dispatch path:
#      the reconciler fires this directly, so mute labels cannot stall the
#      loop
#
# The guard derives the leg: dispatch input leg > label agent:rework >
# label agent:review > assignee/agent:dev (dev). Each leg runs the dmtools
# agent config named by RUNNER_*: dev (story/bug) develops from the issue
# body, review produces a machine PR review verdict, rework fixes the
# linked PR by the review threads.
#
# gh-1065/gh-1073: issues events are deduped before the leg fires — one
# human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits MULTIPLE
# issues events, and without the `dedup` probe job each event spawned its
# own teammate run (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061
# three). The probe is transport only; the decision is the unit-tested
# pure module js/common/teammateEventDedup.js, shipped in the agents pack
# the runner leg mounts (dmtools-agents checkout). The probe FAILS OPEN on
# errors, so a broken check never swallows the only trigger.
name: 'AI Teammate'

# Run title carries the EFFECTIVE anchor (owner 2026-09-27, live: dmd run
# 36333172145): a PR-anchored SM dispatch (#544/#687 — inputs.pr set,
# inputs.issue empty) must title '▶ rework (SM) · pr-266', never the
# malformed '▶ rework (SM) · gh- · gh-: '. (inputs.pr || '') guards the
# label-event path, where inputs are null — null != '' would be TRUE and
# render 'pr-' for ordinary issue events.
#
# gh-1065/gh-1073: the issues-event title ALSO carries the LEG — the
# strongest arming label on the issue (rework > review > pr_approved →
# review > dev), not the label written by THIS event: assign-while-labels-
# change emits a bare `assigned` event whose github.event.label.name is
# empty. legOfRunName (js/common/teammateEventDedup.js) parses this emoji
# title family, so a COMPLETED owner stays title-precise: the strict
# completed-owner leg rule (a leg-less completed run never swallows a
# KNOWN new leg) can only work when real leg runs carry their leg here.
run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework') ||
      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review') ||
      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'pr_approved') && '🔍 review') ||
      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:dev') && '⚒️ dev') ||
      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:develop') && '⚒️ dev') ||
      github.event.label.name || '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (#544/#687) — the SM dispatches review/rework with pr instead of issue when the PR has no resolvable LOCAL issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: write

env:
  AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
  # ── adapt per target repo ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  RUNNER_STORY: dmtools-agents/story_development.json
  RUNNER_BUG: dmtools-agents/bug_development.json
  RUNNER_REVIEW: dmtools-agents/pr_review.json
  RUNNER_REWORK: dmtools-agents/pr_rework.json
  DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF: main
  DMTOOLS_VERSION: v0.1.5
  FA_VERSION: latest
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Secrets expected: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT), plus the AI provider key
  # referenced by the runner configs (e.g. ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY).

jobs:

    # the leg's own lifecycle labels (status:*, ai_developed, ...) — and

    # guard allocated a runner on each lifecycle-label write only to decide
    # run=false (the self-retrigger no-op burn). `assigned` and the arming

    if: >-

      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
      runner: ${{ steps.check.outputs.runner }}
      kind: ${{ steps.check.outputs.kind }}
    steps:
      - name: Decide whether this event is for the agent
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
          ASSIGNEES: ${{ join(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, ' ') }}
          LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}
          INPUT_LEG: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}
        run: |

            ASSIGNEES="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"
          fi

          if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then

          fi
